items.question: Which method best helps you learn about classification?
options: Observe or use evidence, connect it to the concept, and explain the conclusion.

items.question: Explain classification and give one everyday example.
items.answer: A strong answer gives an accurate explanation and a relevant example.

items.question: Apply classification to a new everyday situation. What would you observe or use as evidence?
items.expected_response: Relevant evidence followed by a reasoned conclusion.

items.question: What best demonstrates mastery of 'Diversity in the Living World'?
options: Use major ideas independently in a new situation and explain the reasoning.
Finish the lesson without checking understanding.

flashcards.back: Define classification, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define plant diversity, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define animal diversity, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define adaptation, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore classification
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on classification. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where plant diversity is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach adaptation to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
